answer: Derivation-linked credential scarcity. Each agent identity embeds a spendable credit whose cipher unlocks only when its recent task history matches the ledger's expected work distribution; mismatches stall the credit. Cloning forces the attacker to re-derive that history per identity, costing real compute and failed-task penalties, so a sybil farm pays roughly N times honest onboarding. An ivory audit trail of past outputs must verify before the credit clears, making honest continuation cheaper than a fresh oasis of clones.
